source.title: Multi-task representations in human cortex transform along a sensory-to-motor hierarchy

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity among cortical regions and between ANN layers and brain regions, but does not test convergence between independently trained models, scale-related alignment, or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The ANN and brain representational-similarity results are related findings, but they do not measure the convergence specified by the claim versions. Other results, including dimensionality and weight properties, do not bear directly on the claim. No results from cited work are included.
record.test_reason: The study maps representational alignment among human cortical regions and compares RSMs of a small linear ANN (trained to map visual-parcel fMRI to motor-parcel fMRI) with brain RSMs under rich vs lazy initialization. It does not compare independently trained models across scale, architecture or modality. It does not report cross-seed feature sharing, cross-model mapping, or universal features. Brain-model similarity and within-network inter-layer alignment are related constructs, not the convergence any version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that cortical multi-task representations compress then expand along a sensory-association-motor gradient. Only rich-regime training of the ANN reproduced this pattern and gave representations more similar to the brain's, with structured layer-by-layer transformations. They draw no conclusions about convergence across independently trained models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA and cosine similarity to study multi-task representations in human cortex and trained ANN layers; it does not reproduce a method testing convergence among independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: ANN representational patterns differed between rich and lazy weight-initialization regimes. The study also reports task-condition subsampling analyses for dimensionality and compression-then-expansion, not for convergence between models.

fits_no_version.finding: A linear ANN trained in the rich regime (small initialization SD) had RSMs more similar to cortical RSMs than one trained in the lazy regime (cosine 0.42 vs 0.37). Within the ANN, lazier initialization gave higher mean inter-layer alignment, with little layer-wise structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training regime set by initialization scale changes a network's representational similarity to brain regions and to its own layers. This concerns model-brain correspondence, not convergence across independently trained models.

record.code_released: The authors state that code will be made publicly available on GitHub; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The ANN analysis uses a specific linear feedforward architecture and visual-to-motor fMRI transformation. The reported alignment comparisons concern ANN layers and cortical regions, not independently trained models; the study does not test scale or performance-related convergence.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported results concern representational dimensionality, segregation, weight properties, or model fit and are not direct measurements of the claim’s convergence subject.

untested.parts: Alignment of independently trained models of different architecture, objective or data as scale and capability grow.
Vision-language alignment on paired image-caption data.
Feature or subspace sharing across seeds. The 20 seeds per initialization are averaged, not compared with each other.
Mapping or stitching between models' representations.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of model-model convergence on the similarity metric, its settings or the inputs. The authors only mention alternative RA metrics as future work.
Whether model-model alignment is incomplete or explained by shared data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The model is a 10-layer tied-weight linear ANN trained per subject on fMRI parcel activations. Seeds are pooled, never compared with each other. T6/discusses is appropriate, and arguably T6 alone since the claim is not discussed at all.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities become more aligned as size and capability increase.
Alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions as model performance changes.
Whether independently initialized networks share features or subspaces across seeds.
Whether representations can be mapped or stitched across models, including by linear maps, relative representations, or without paired data.
Whether interpretable features or circuits recur across different models.
Whether convergence between independently trained models changes with similarity metric, settings, or input distribution.
Whether alignment between independently trained models is incomplete or explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: 10-layer linear feedforward ANN
rows.operation_detail: Compared ANN layer RSMs with cortical parcel RSMs using cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity of ANN-layer and empirical brain RSMs
rows.uncertainty: t198=15.28, p<10e-34 for rich vs. lazy comparison
rows.locator: Results, “Compression-then-expansion of task representations in a feedforward ANN emerges during rich training”; Fig. 6e
rows.note: Aggregate comparison across ANN layers and cortical parcel RSMs; the reported value is for the rich regime.
rows.check: ANN-to-brain RSM similarity (rich regime, cosine 0.42) is model-brain correspondence, not convergence between independently trained models. Values are averaged over 20 seeds per initialization, with no cross-seed comparison.

rows.subject: 10-layer linear feedforward ANN
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between RSMs of pairs of ANN layers.
rows.measure: Mean inter-layer representational alignment (cosine similarity of layer RSMs)
rows.baseline: lazy regime; the text reports the rich-versus-lazy difference
rows.value: rich vs. lazy cosine difference=-0.12; higher/lazier weight initialization produced greater overall RA
rows.locator: Results, “Richly trained ANNs learn hierarchical representational transformations”; Fig. 7d-e
rows.note: This is alignment among layers of the ANN, not alignment among independently trained models.
rows.check: Inter-layer alignment within one network. The value is the rich-minus-lazy difference (-0.12), not a lazy baseline. This is not cross-model alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
